title: A Koi-smic fish
caption: The Gum 3 nebula, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Red and pink clouds mix with blue in this bright view of the Gum 3 nebula, and part of it resembles a koi fish. Just to the right of the brightest region, the pink fish, a patch of sky seems oddly empty of stars.

Each color has its own cause. Intense ultraviolet light from nearby young stars strikes hydrogen atoms in the cloud, which then give off visible light at very specific colors, which appear as reds and pinks. Tiny dust particles also reflect starlight, especially blue light, for the same reason Earth's sky looks blue.

The empty-looking patch is not really short of stars. A large knot of dust sits there, soaking up visible light and screening the stars beyond it. Gum 3 is a cloud of gas and dust between the constellations Monoceros and Canis Major, named after the Australian astronomer Colin Stanley Gum.

understand.summary: The VLT Survey Telescope's OmegaCAM camera took this visible-light image. The filter details and color mapping aren't published.
understand.eye: Long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so these colors would appear much fainter, if at all, to a viewer.

explore: Gum cataloged 84 nebulae in the southern sky. The picture was taken with the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory, whose OmegaCAM camera has 268 megapixels and is built to map wide swathes of the southern sky in visible light.
alt: A brightly colored nebula of red, pink and blue clouds, part shaped like a koi fish, with a dark, star-poor patch beside it.
